subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw support declarative per-job cron files, and should that be a runtime `jobs.d` store or an import/reconcile artifact feeding SQLite?
rationale: Current code and policy make SQLite the canonical cron runtime store, while this request adds new config/storage semantics with migration, identity, deletion, and path-safety implications that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Reconcile Into SQLite
options.body: Add a documented deterministic import/export or reconcile surface that validates per-job JSON and writes canonical SQLite rows without making file polling the runtime store.

options.title: Runtime Directory Store
options.body: Add a new directory-backed cron store mode with explicit migration, symlink, path-safety, stable filename, and upgrade semantics owned by maintainers.

options.title: Decline Core Storage Mode
options.body: Keep supported cron management on the CLI/Gateway API and leave declarative file merging to external user-side tooling for now.

recommendation.title: Reconcile Into SQLite
recommendation.body: Add a documented deterministic import/export or reconcile surface that validates per-job JSON and writes canonical SQLite rows without making file polling the runtime store.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite cron persistence and current storage boundary most directly trace through steipete's merged cron store work and docs updates.
